source: create a game where users cam fly all kinds of vehicles & they will get points after hitting the CP written boards on various similar looking buildings.

image_prompt.text: Wide clear flight corridors between the buildings, standing in for the roads a ground vehicle sim would use
The shared field of scoring targets the whole server draws from
a cluster of similar-looking buildings spread across open ground, each carrying a large CP board on its facade, readable from the air

layout_placement.text: scoring trigger volumes on each CP board that award points when a flying vehicle hits them

notes: Racing's boundary rule decided this: there is no lap and no finish line, so a vehicle game routes to Simulation rather than Racing. It is a poor fit - the checkpoint-and-score loop is competitive and Vehicle Sim is explicitly cooperative with no scoring.
Nothing in Simulation expresses a checkpoint, a scoring trigger, or flight, which are the three things this prompt is made of.
'All kinds of vehicles' was left open; the map is framed for aircraft.

open_questions.ask: No theme was stated - modern city, military airfield, or something stylized?
Is this a timed score attack, a race between players to the highest score, or endless free flight?

coverage_missing.ask: Timed score attack, competition between players, or endless free flight?
How many buildings and how far apart - a few blocks, or a landscape you fly across for minutes?
Which flying vehicles - planes, helicopters, jetpacks, all of them?

answers.ask: No theme was stated - modern city, military airfield, or something stylized?
answers.answer: Use a small modern city with similar-looking buildings and rooftop/side checkpoint boards.

answers.ask: Is this a timed score attack, a race between players to the highest score, or endless free flight?
answers.answer: Make it endless free flight: players earn points whenever they hit checkpoint boards, with their score tracked on a leaderboard.
